name: Malik Muhammad Jayasi
credit: Queen Nagamati talks to her parrot, an illustrated manuscript folio of the Padmavat (North India, c. 1750; Library of Congress) · An artifact, shown because no authentic likeness of the poet exists · Public domain (Wikimedia Commons)
bio: Malik Muhammad Jayasi (c. 1477–1542) was a Sufi poet who wrote in Awadhi, the eastern dialect of Hindi, and who is traditionally associated with the town of Jais in Awadh, from which his name is taken. His works were first written in the Persian script, and the Hindi tradition counts him among the foremost poets of the Sufi love-romance, the premakhyan.

His best known poem is the Padmavat, composed in 1540. It tells, in seven-line chaupai stanzas closed by a couplet, how King Ratansen of Chittor wins the Sinhala princess Padmavati and loses her to the siege of the Delhi sultan Alauddin; the story is read as an allegory of the soul's search for the divine. The text here is the Padmavat in Ramchandra Shukla's edition, the Jayasi Granthavali (1924), from the Hindi Wikisource transcription.
